added.heading: You were added to {workspace}
added.reason: You got this email because a server admin of {site} added this address. If you didn't expect it, you can ignore it.
added.subject: You were added to {workspace} on {site}
added.text: {who} added you to {workspace} on {site} as {role}: answer and follow up on the calls its assistant takes.
addedNotice.reason: You got this email because a server admin of {site} added you. If you didn't expect it, tell the workspace's owner.
addedToWorkspace.note: The link works for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Enter this email address on the sign-in page and we send you a code.
addedToWorkspace.preheader: {inviter} added you as {role}. Sign in with this address to join.
adminAlert.adminGranted.subject: New server admin on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.billingDispute.next: {kind, select, dispute {Answer the dispute in the Stripe Dashboard. If it is won, the amount goes back on the balance.} other {Refunding the charge now avoids the dispute fee.}}
adminAlert.billingDispute.subject: {kind, select, dispute {A card dispute} other {An early fraud warning}} on {brand}: bill {bill} suspended
adminAlert.billingDispute.text: {kind, select, dispute {A customer disputed a charge.} other {A card issuer reported a charge as fraud.}} The bill is suspended: its calls get the fixed line until an instance admin resumes it.
adminAlert.billingDisputeClosed.subject: {lifted, select, yes {A dispute on {brand} is settled: bill {bill} is resumed} other {A dispute on {brand} closed: bill {bill} stays suspended}}
adminAlert.billingDisputeClosed.text: {lifted, select, yes {Stripe settled the dispute or fraud warning in our favour. Anything taken off the balance is back, and nothing else holds the bill, so it is resumed.} other {The dispute or fraud warning closed, but the bill stays suspended: the dispute was lost, or something else still holds it. Check the bill in Server admin › Billing and resume it there when it is clear.}}
adminAlert.billingLifecycleFailed.next: The next run in an hour tries them again. If a step keeps failing, check the Stripe keys and the server log.
adminAlert.billingLifecycleFailed.subjec: Dunning on {brand}: {count, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} failed
adminAlert.billingLifecycleFailed.text: The hourly dunning job (suspending, canceling, releasing numbers) could not finish these steps:
adminAlert.billingPeriodsFailed.next: The next run in an hour tries them again. If a step keeps failing, check the Stripe keys and the server log.
adminAlert.billingPeriodsFailed.subject: Billing periods on {brand}: {count, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} failed
adminAlert.billingPeriodsFailed.text: The hourly billing job (periods, extra numbers, renewal reminders) could not finish these steps:
adminAlert.billingReconcile.kind: {kind, select, missed_events {Events not received} events_truncated {Events not compared (more than the run reads)} failed_events {Events that keep failing} run_failed {The comparison could not run} status {Status} period {Billing period} quantity {Workspace seats} payment_method {Payment method} refund {A refund without its ledger entry, posted now} other {Other}}
adminAlert.billingReconcile.nightly: Events that were not received are processed now. The rest needs a look in Server admin and the Stripe Dashboard.
adminAlert.billingReconcile.subject: Billing on {brand} differs from Stripe: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}}
adminAlert.billingReconcile.text: The nightly comparison of the bills with Stripe found these differences:
adminAlert.billingRules.reset: every rule is back to its default
adminAlert.billingRules.subject: The billing rules were changed
adminAlert.billingRules.text: {actor} changed this install's billing rules (Server admin › Billing): {fields}. Reason given: {reason}
adminAlert.billingSwitch.subject: Billing was turned {on, select, yes {on} other {off}}
adminAlert.billingSwitch.text: {actor} turned billing {on, select, yes {on, with the Stripe account {account} in {mode} mode: businesses on this install are charged} other {off: nothing is charged and no card is used}} (Server admin › Billing › Stripe).
adminAlert.billingUnusable.fix: Run the migrations again, or fix the keys in Server admin › Providers › Stripe. You get this email once; billing comes back on its own once it works.
adminAlert.billingUnusable.subject: Billing on {brand} is switched on but not working
adminAlert.billingUnusable.text: {reason, select, guards {The database rules that keep the billing ledger correct are missing, changed or could not be checked.} other {The Stripe keys are missing, or this server does not allow them.}} Until billing works again, calls of workspaces on a bill are refused and filed as missed.
adminAlert.cappedCall.check: Check the call in Server admin and with the carrier. If it really ran that long, credit or charge the difference by hand.
adminAlert.cappedCall.subject: A call on {brand} was billed less than it reported
adminAlert.cappedCall.text: A call reported {reported} seconds, more than its time limit plus the grace allows, so it was billed for {billed} seconds. A wrong duration, a stuck call or a call the stale sweep did not end can cause this.
adminAlert.catalogSync.check: The Stripe key needs write access to Products and Prices, and the lookup keys ws_monthly, ws_yearly, partner_monthly and partner_yearly must not belong to another product. Test the key in Server admin › Billing › Stripe, then save the prices again.
adminAlert.catalogSync.lastSynced: New Checkouts keep selling the prices of the last update that worked, and Buy minutes keeps working.
adminAlert.catalogSync.neverSynced: The prices were never set up in this Stripe account, so nobody can start a trial or a plan until this is fixed. Buy minutes keeps working.
adminAlert.catalogSync.subject: Stripe products and prices on {brand} could not be updated
adminAlert.catalogSync.text: The billing prices or the product name were saved, but Stripe refused to update the products and plan prices ({code}).
adminAlert.checkAudit: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Audit log.
adminAlert.checkBilling: Check it under Server admin › Billing.
adminAlert.checkProviders: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Providers and Audit log.
adminAlert.checkStripe: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Billing and Audit log.
adminAlert.checkUsers: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Users and Audit log.
adminAlert.checkoutExtra.refund: It was paid: refund the payment in Stripe.
adminAlert.checkoutExtra.subject: An extra Checkout on {brand} was canceled
adminAlert.checkoutExtra.text: Bill {bill} completed Checkout {session} after its plan had already started. Its subscription {subscription} was canceled at once, so it charges nothing more.
adminAlert.checkoutExtra.trial: It was a trial, so nothing was charged. Nothing to do.
adminAlert.checkoutRefused.check: Check the session and the customer in Stripe: refund anything that was charged, and cancel a subscription that still runs.
adminAlert.checkoutRefused.subject: A Checkout on {brand} was refused
adminAlert.checkoutRefused.text: Checkout {session} of bill {bill} was completed in Stripe, and the server did not apply it: {reason}
adminAlert.checkoutSetup.check: Run the billing bootstrap (it makes the card-only payment method configuration, the customer portal and the webhook endpoint; the prices are made by the app when billing is turned on or the prices are saved), then check the Stripe keys and their permissions in Server admin › Billing › Stripe.
adminAlert.checkoutSetup.subject: Checkout on {brand} could not start
adminAlert.checkoutSetup.text: A bill owner tried to start Checkout, and Stripe refused it because of the setup ({code}). Nobody can start a trial or buy minutes until this is fixed; the owner was asked to try again later.
adminAlert.dataPurgeFailed.next: The next run tomorrow tries them again. If they keep failing, check the recording storage and the server log: the privacy policy promises this deletion.
adminAlert.dataPurgeFailed.subject: Data deletion on {brand}: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} not deleted
adminAlert.dataPurgeFailed.text: The daily job {job} could not delete these, so deleted calls or the data of canceled workspaces are kept longer than promised:
adminAlert.enrolmentIssued.subject: Passkey enrolment code issued on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.enrolmentIssued.text: {actor} issued a one-time code for the first passkey of {email}, an instance admin without a passkey. Nothing was removed and their sessions and AI agent setup links keep working.
adminAlert.extraCallsSync.fix: Look the subscription up in Stripe and set the extra-calls item to the number the bill shows in Server admin › Billing. The nightly reconciliation lists the difference until then.
adminAlert.extraCallsSync.subject: Extra calls on {brand} could not be updated in Stripe
adminAlert.extraCallsSync.text: The extra calls at the same time of bill {bill} changed, but Stripe could not be updated. Stripe now charges for a different number of extra calls than the bill has.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.failed: The nightly billing check stopped with an error, so the ledger was not compared tonight. The server log has the error.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.failedSubject: The billing check on {brand} could not run
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.guards: Billing is off: the database rules that keep the ledger correct are missing, disabled or changed. Run the migrations again; billing comes back at the next good check.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.kind: {kind, select, balance {Balance} reserved {Reserved for running calls} counter_allowance {Included minutes used} counter_usage {Usage this period} uncredited {Recharge not credited} other {Other}}
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.nightly: The billing check runs every night; you get this email each night until it is fixed.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.subject: Billing check on {brand}: {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}} found
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.sums: These stored sums do not match the ledger (amounts in millionths of a dollar):
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.uncredited: Bill {bill}: recharge {recharge} is paid but the balance was not credited
adminAlert.partnerBrand.check: Check that the name, logo, support email and links are the partner's own and borrow no one else's. Server admin › Partners approves the change or removes the brand.
adminAlert.partnerBrand.name: Product name
adminAlert.partnerBrand.subject: Partner brand to review on {brand}: {partner}
adminAlert.partnerBrand.text: The white-label partner {partner} changed the brand its clients see in the app and in emails. Until a server admin approves the change, its clients and their emails keep the approved version.
adminAlert.partnerDomain.check: Check that the address is the partner's own and imitates no one else's. Server admin › Partners removes it at once.
adminAlert.partnerDomain.subject: Partner address on {brand}: {partner}
adminAlert.partnerDomain.text: The white-label partner {partner} added its own address. Once its DNS records are in, its clients sign in there.
adminAlert.partnerSender.check: Check that the domain is the partner's own and imitates no one else's. Server admin › Partners removes the sender.
adminAlert.partnerSender.subject: Partner sender domain on {brand}: {partner}
adminAlert.partnerSender.text: The white-label partner {partner} added its own sender address. Once its DNS records are verified, its clients' emails come from it.
adminAlert.partnerSignUp.check: Check that the company is real and that its name borrows no one else's. Server admin › Partners approves it.
adminAlert.partnerSignUp.subject: New partner waiting for approval on {brand}: {partner}
adminAlert.partnerSignUp.text: {partner} signed up for White-label Cloud. It can start its plan and add client workspaces now. Its brand in its clients' emails and its own domain wait for a server admin's approval.
adminAlert.passkeysReset.admin: They are an instance admin and got a new enrolment code for their first passkey.
adminAlert.passkeysReset.subject: Passkeys reset on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.passkeysReset.text: {actor} removed every passkey of {email} ({count, plural, one {# removed} other {# removed}}) and ended their sessions and AI agent setup links.
adminAlert.portalSync.check: Give the restricted key "Write" on Customer portal in Stripe, or run the billing bootstrap once, then test the key in Server admin › Providers › Stripe and save the billing settings again.
adminAlert.portalSync.subject: The Stripe customer portal on {brand} could not be updated
adminAlert.portalSync.text: The billing settings were saved, but Stripe refused to set up the customer portal ({code}). The portal must offer invoices and cards only, never cancel or plan changes; while it offers them, bill owners cannot open it.
adminAlert.providerFailure.impact: Calls or emails that need it may not work until it is fixed. Server admin › Providers shows the latest failure; a successful test or call clears it.
adminAlert.providerFailure.once: You get this email once per failure, not for every call.
adminAlert.providerFailure.subject: {provider} is failing on {brand}: {reason, select, quota {quota or credit used up} auth {key rejected} permission {missing permission} not_found {not found} config {setting refused} network {not reachable} timeout {no answer in time} no_output {answered with nothing} other {failing}}
adminAlert.reason: You got this email because you are a server admin of {site}. Every server admin gets these alerts.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.next: Check the invoice in the Stripe Dashboard. If the customer really paid, credit the bill by hand for this recharge attempt (billing.credit with the recharge id), so it can never be credited twice; otherwise nothing needs to happen.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.reason: {reason, select, out_of_band {Stripe shows the recharge invoice as paid, but it was marked paid outside Stripe.} not_charged {Stripe shows the recharge invoice as paid, but card payments do not cover its total (a customer credit balance or a partial payment).} discounted {The recharge invoice has a discount, so the card paid less than the recharge.} not_covered {The recharge invoice has a credit or negative line, or its total before tax is less than the recharge, so what was paid does not cover the recharge.} amount_mismatch {The recharge invoice's amount is not the amount of the recharge attempt.} no_line {The recharge invoice has no line for this recharge attempt.} currency {The recharge invoice is not in US dollars.} customer_mismatch {The recharge invoice belongs to another Stripe customer than the bill.} canceled {The recharge attempt was canceled, but its invoice was paid.} other {The recharge invoice did not pass the payment checks.}} Nothing was added to the balance.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.subject: A paid recharge on {brand} was not credited
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.check: Check the Stripe keys and their permissions in Server admin › Providers › Stripe, and the customer in the Stripe Dashboard.
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.subject: A recharge on {brand} failed on the Stripe setup
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.text: Stripe refused the recharge ({code}): the keys, their permissions or the customer are not right. The attempt was canceled and the bill owner was not told. Until this is fixed, every recharge fails the same way.
adminAlert.seatsSync.fix: Look the subscription up in Stripe and set the seat item to the number of workspaces the bill shows in Server admin › Billing. The next client change sets it too; the nightly reconciliation lists the difference until then.
adminAlert.seatsSync.subject: Partner seats on {brand} could not be updated in Stripe
adminAlert.seatsSync.text: A client workspace joined or left partner bill {bill}, but Stripe could not be updated after several tries. Stripe now charges for a different number of seats than the bill has.
adminAlert.selfServe.subject: Self-serve sign-up was turned {on, select, yes {on} other {off}}
adminAlert.selfServe.text: {actor} turned self-serve sign-up {on, select, yes {on: anyone can sign up and start a trial with a card} other {off: only server admins create workspaces}} (Server admin › Billing). Reason given: {reason}
adminAlert.settings.agentEnds: That admin ends the link with End access on the setup page; disabling the admin ends it too.
adminAlert.settings.moneyText: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} other {changed the {provider} settings}} (Server admin › Billing). They control billing: charges, refunds and customers.
adminAlert.settings.moneyTextAgent: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} other {changed the {provider} settings}} through the AI agent setup link {prefix}…{hasMade, select, yes {, made {made}} other {}}. They control billing: charges, refunds and customers.
adminAlert.settings.subject: {change, select, changed {{provider} settings changed} removed {{provider} settings removed} switched {Email now sent with {provider}} other {Email provider pick cleared}}{agent, select, yes { by an AI agent} other {}}
adminAlert.settings.text: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} switched {switched email to {provider}} other {cleared which email provider sends}} (Server admin › Providers). They decide how people sign in or get sign-in codes.
adminAlert.settings.textAgent: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} switched {switched email to {provider}} other {cleared which email provider sends}} through the AI agent setup link {prefix}…{hasMade, select, yes {, made {made}} other {}}. They decide how people sign in or get sign-in codes.
adminAlert.signIn.ifNot: If this was them, nothing to do. If not, someone has their passkey, authenticator app or device: sign in with your own passkey, then in Server admin › Users disable the account and reset its passkeys.
adminAlert.signIn.subject: Admin sign-in from a new device on {brand}: {who}
adminAlert.signIn.text: {method, select, passkey {{who}, a server admin, confirmed with their passkey from a device not seen before for them.} authenticator {{who}, a server admin, confirmed with their authenticator app from a device not seen before for them.} password {{who}, a server admin, signed in with a password from a device not seen before for them.} email_code {{who}, a server admin, signed in with an email code from a device not seen before for them.} email_link {{who}, a server admin, signed in with an email link from a device not seen before for them.} provider {{who}, a server admin, signed in with {provider} from a device not seen before for them.} unknown {{who}, a server admin, signed in with a sign-in method this server does not recognise from a device not seen before for them.} other {{who}, a server admin, signed in with “{how}” from a device not seen before for them.}}
adminAlert.signupCap.check: Check Server admin › Audit log and the new accounts for a pattern (one domain, one network). If the sign-ups are real, raise codesPerInstallHour in the sign-up rules; to stop them, turn self-serve sign-up off.
adminAlert.signupCap.subject: Sign-up on {brand} reached its hourly limit
adminAlert.signupCap.text: The sign-up page asked for {cap} email codes in the last hour, the most this server sends. More sign-up codes are refused until the hour is over; existing accounts sign in as before.
adminAlert.signupKept.check: Look the bill up in Server admin › Billing and the subscription in Stripe. If the customer paid or started a trial, process their checkout.session.completed event again; otherwise cancel the subscription in Stripe. This email comes every day until the bill no longer waits.
adminAlert.signupKept.inStripe.check: Look the customer up in Stripe and the billing webhook's deliveries. If the customer paid or started a trial, process their checkout.session.completed event again; otherwise cancel the subscription in Stripe. This email comes every day until the bill no longer waits.
adminAlert.signupKept.inStripe.text: The daily sign-up sweep did not delete this bill: it still waits for Checkout in Linedesk, but in Stripe its customer has a running subscription or a completed Checkout. Most likely the Checkout webhook was not applied yet (delayed, or the webhook endpoint failed). It is kept until someone looks.
adminAlert.signupKept.stripeError.check: Check the Stripe keys in Server admin › Providers › Stripe and Stripe's status. This email comes on every run that cannot reach Stripe.
adminAlert.signupKept.stripeError.subjec: The sign-up sweep on {brand} could not ask Stripe about a waiting sign-up
adminAlert.signupKept.stripeError.text: The daily sign-up sweep did not delete this bill, which still waits for Checkout: Stripe could not be asked whether its customer has a subscription or a completed Checkout. Nothing was deleted; the next run tries again.
adminAlert.signupKept.subject: A sign-up on {brand} waits for Checkout but has a Stripe subscription
adminAlert.signupKept.text: The daily sign-up sweep did not delete this bill: it still waits for Checkout, but a Stripe subscription is linked to it or its Checkout was confirmed. It is kept until someone looks.
adminAlert.signupRules.botCheckOff: The bot check is now OFF: anyone, bots included, can ask for sign-up codes. Only the rate limits protect this install.
adminAlert.signupRules.field.codesPerAdd: Sign-up codes per email address, per day
Sign-up codes per email address, per hour
adminAlert.signupRules.field.codesPerIns: Sign-up codes on this server, per hour
adminAlert.signupRules.field.reviewRiskL: Hold for review at Radar risk
adminAlert.signupRules.field.trialNumber: Phone numbers per workspace in the trial
adminAlert.signupRules.noReview: No Radar risk level holds a trial for review now: risky cards can buy phone numbers at once.
adminAlert.signupRules.opened: Sign-up is now open: anyone can sign up and start a trial with a card.
adminAlert.signupRules.subject: The sign-up rules were changed
adminAlert.signupRules.subjectOpened: Sign-up is now open: the sign-up rules were changed
adminAlert.signupRules.text: {actor} changed this install's sign-up rules (Server admin › Billing). Reason given: {reason}
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.next: Fix the cause (Stripe keys, the ledger guards, an unknown period), then process it again with billing.reprocessEvent. It is applied once, however often it runs.
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.subject: A Stripe event on {brand} could not be processed
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.text: Billing tried to process this Stripe event {attempts} times and failed each time. Until it is processed, what it reports (a payment, a status change) is not applied to the bill.
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.check: Look the invoices up in Stripe (metadata billing_recharge_id) and the billing webhook's deliveries.
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.subject: {count, plural, one {# recharge} other {# recharges}} on {brand} still waiting to be settled
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.text: These recharge attempts have been pending for more than 2 hours. While one is pending, its bill gets no new automatic recharge, and once the balance runs out its calls are refused.
appPush.title: {brand} call: {caller}
assigned.reason: You got this email because a teammate in {workspace} assigned you a call.
assigned.subject: {by} assigned you a call: {topic}
authenticatorChanged.heading: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added} other {The authenticator app was removed}}
authenticatorChanged.notYou: If it wasn't you, ask another server admin of your {brand} to reset your passkeys (Server admin › Users, your name, Reset passkeys): that also removes the authenticator app. Then sign in and add your own again.
authenticatorChanged.subject: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added to} other {The authenticator app was removed from}} your {brand} account
authenticatorChanged.text: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added to your {brand} account at {site}. It opens Server admin like your passkey.} other {The authenticator app was removed from your {brand} account at {site}.}}
billing.activationNudge.deleted: If you don't start by {date}, we delete this sign-up and what you set up.
billing.activationNudge.noCharge: Nothing is charged when you start. We email you before the first charge, and you can cancel any time before it.
billing.activationNudge.reason: You got this email because you signed up on {site} and have not started yet. It is the only reminder we send about it.
billing.activationNudge.subject: One step left: start your {brand} free trial
billing.activationNudge.subjectPlan: One step left: start your {brand} plan
billing.activationNudge.text: {assistant} is almost ready to answer calls for {workspace}. Start your {days}-day free trial to get your phone number and turn on real calls.
billing.activationNudge.textPlan: {assistant} is almost ready to answer calls for {workspace}. Start your plan to get your phone number and turn on real calls.
billing.busyLine.add: Each {step} more calls at the same time cost {price} a month. You can pick another amount in Settings › Billing.
billing.busyLine.afterTrial: You can add more calls at the same time once your plan is paid, after the trial.
billing.busyLine.button: Add {step} more lines for {price} a month
billing.busyLine.once: We send this at most once a day per workspace.
billing.busyLine.subject: {callers, plural, one {A caller} other {# callers}} got a busy line at {workspace}
billing.busyLine.text: On {date}, {workspace} was already on {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}} at the same time, so {callers, plural, one {a caller} other {# callers}} heard that you'll call back. They are in your inbox as missed calls, with their numbers.
billing.canceled.data: Your inbox stays readable and can be exported until {dataDate}.
billing.canceled.numbers: Your phone numbers are kept until {date}. To keep a number, port it to another carrier before then: Settings › Billing shows the port-out details. After that date the numbers are released.
billing.canceled.subject: Your {brand} plan was canceled
billing.canceled.text: Your plan fee stayed unpaid for 30 days, so your plan was canceled. Calls are no longer answered.
billing.capReached.effect: Calls go on until the balance is {buffer} below zero; then the assistant stops answering new calls. Buy minutes or raise the cap in Settings › Billing to keep it answering.
billing.capReached.recharged: Automatic recharges came to {recharged} this month (UTC); the smallest recharge is {minimum}.
billing.capReached.subject: Your {brand} balance reached its monthly recharge cap
billing.capReached.text: What is left under your monthly recharge cap of {cap} is less than the smallest recharge, so no more automatic recharges happen this month (UTC).
billing.dunningReminder.subject: Reminder: your {brand} plan is still unpaid
billing.dunningReminder.text: Your plan fee is still unpaid, so your assistant does not answer calls.
billing.lowBalance.effect: When the balance runs out, the assistant stops answering new calls. Buy minutes or turn auto-recharge on in Settings › Billing.
billing.lowBalance.subject: Your {brand} balance is low
billing.lowBalance.text: Your prepaid balance is down to {balance}, and auto-recharge is off.
billing.managerChanged.cancel: The plan ends on {date}. Until then calls are answered as before, and the plan can be resumed in Settings › Billing.
billing.managerChanged.cancelNoDate: The plan ends at the end of the current period. Until then it can be resumed in Settings › Billing.
billing.managerChanged.card: From now on the bill is charged to the {brand} card ending in {last4}.
billing.managerChanged.cardUnknown: From now on the bill is charged to the new card.
billing.managerChanged.extraCalls: Extra calls at the same time: {from} before, {to} now.
billing.managerChanged.intervalMonth: From now on the plan is paid monthly. Nothing is charged before the free trial ends.
billing.managerChanged.intervalYear: From now on the plan is paid yearly. Nothing is charged before the free trial ends.
billing.managerChanged.notExpected: Not what you expected? Check Settings › Billing and talk to {who}.
billing.managerChanged.resume: The plan no longer ends: it renews as before.
billing.managerChanged.subject.extraCall: {who} changed the calls at the same time for {workspace}
billing.managerChanged.subject.interval: {who} changed how the plan for {workspace} is paid
billing.managerChanged.text: {by} manages the bill of {workspace} with you and made this change on {when}. You pay this bill, so we let you know.
billing.numberUnpaid.effect: Until it is paid, calls to {number} are not answered by the assistant. Buy minutes in Settings › Billing and the month is paid within the hour. If it stays unpaid, the number is released on {date}.
billing.numberUnpaid.subject: {number} on {brand} is not paid for this month
billing.numberUnpaid.text: This month of your extra number {number} ({price}) could not be paid from your prepaid balance: the balance is too low and no automatic recharge can run.
billing.numbersReleased.subject: Your {brand} phone numbers were released
billing.numbersReleased.text: Your plan was canceled 30 days ago, so {count, plural, one {this number was} other {these numbers were}} released and can no longer be ported:
billing.planMinutesLow.subject: You used {used} of your {included} included minutes this month
billing.planMinutesLow.text: {left, plural, one {# minute is} other {# minutes are}} left this month. After that, calls need call credit, and auto-recharge is off.
billing.portOutRequested.notYou: If you did not ask for this, contact the team that runs {brand} right away: a port-out moves the number for good.
billing.portOutRequested.subject: A port-out of {number} was requested
billing.portOutRequested.text: Another carrier asked to move {number} away from {brand}. Once the port completes, calls to it no longer reach your assistant.
billing.reason: You got this email because you pay for a bill on {site}.
billing.rechargeFailed.effect: Calls go on until the balance is {buffer} below zero; then the assistant stops answering new calls. No new recharge is tried until you update your card or retry it in Settings › Billing.
billing.rechargeFailed.subject: Your {brand} balance could not be recharged
billing.rechargeFailed.text: We tried to charge {amount} (plus tax where it applies) to your saved card to recharge your prepaid balance, and the payment did not go through.
billing.renewalReminder.autoRechargeOff: Auto-recharge is off: calls beyond the included minutes need balance you buy yourself.
billing.renewalReminder.autoRechargeOn: Auto-recharge stays on: when your prepaid balance falls below {threshold}, we charge {amount} (plus tax where it applies) to the same card, up to your monthly cap.
billing.renewalReminder.cancel: Don't want it to renew? Cancel in Settings › Billing before {date}; your plan then runs until that day.

billing.renewalReminder.subject: Your {brand} plan renews on {date}

billing.trialMinutes.free: Your plan stays free until {date}. Minutes beyond the included ones cost {rate} each.
